court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Aruna Gautam Kamble And Another vs Head Master Rampratap Malpani

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Aruna Gautam Kamble, Kum. Sneha Gautam Kamble (mother and minor daughter)
parties.respondent_defendant: Head Master, Rampratap Malpani Mukbadhir Vidyalaya, Life Insurance Corporation of India, PACL India Ltd., Seema Gautam Kamble, Subodh Gautam Kamble, Jay Gautam Kamble, Ajay Gautam Kamble (school and insurance companies, family members)

facts_of_case: Applicants claim heirship/successor of Gautam Kambale. Applicants Aruna and Sneha had applied Section 372 of the Indian Succession Act, claiming deceased Gautam solemnized marriage with Aruna and they were blessed with daughter Sneha.

legal_principles.principle: A child of a marriage which is null and void under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act is statutorily conferred with legitimacy, irrespective of whether such a child was born before or after commencement of Amending Act 1976.
legal_principles.held: It has been held that in terms of sub-section (1) of Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act, a child of a marriage which is null and void under Section 11 is statutorily conferred with legitimacy.
cited_cases: Revanasiddappa and another Versus Mallikarjun and others, Civil Appeal No.2844 of 2011

legal_principles.principle: The paternity of a child cannot be held legitimate under Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act unless the competent Court decides her paternity.
legal_principles.held: Unless the competent Court decides her paternity, she would not be entitled to any such certificate.
cited_cases: Banarasidass v Teeku Dutta (Mrs) and another (2005) 4 SCC 449

outcome.final_order: The applicants' appeal is allowed. The judgment and order dated 09.06.2020 of the learned Principal District Judge, Nanded, passed in Regular Civil Appeal No.33 of 2014 filed by the applicants and Regular Civil Appeal No.18 of 2014 filed by the respondents are set aside.
